title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Compute each element as the product of all other array elements without using division.

data.text: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is the product of all elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`. You cannot use division.
Build two extra arrays: products of everything to the left and to the right. Multiply them. O(n) time, O(n) space.

data.title: Prefix + Suffix O(n)

data.text: Approach 2: Output Array as One Pass
Reuse the output array for the left products, then run a right-to-left pass accumulating the right product on the fly. O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

data.title: O(n) O(1) Extra

data.caption: The optimized approach stores left products in the result array, then multiplies by right products in a second pass.
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[nums=[1,2,3,4]] --> B[result[0]=1]
    B --> C[result[1]=1]
    C --> D[result[2]=2]
    D --> E[result[3]=6]
    E --> F[right=1]
    F --> G[result[3]*=1 right*=4]
    G --> H[result[2]*=4 right*=3]
    H --> I[result[1]*=12 right*=2]
    I --> J[result[0]*=24]
    J --> K[result=[24,12,8,6]]
    style K fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

data.title: What improved?
data.text: **Time:** O(n) both ways. **Space:** O(n) → O(1) extra by folding the right pass into the result array. This is the classic interview optimization.
